summary: The document describes a green synthesis of 3,4-disubstituted isoxazol-5(4H)-ones using gluconic acid aqueous solution (GAAS) as a recyclable medium. It includes optimization tables for reaction conditions, a general synthesis scheme, and characterization data for nine specific products.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Gluconic acid aqueous solution catalyzed synthesis of 3,4-disubstituted isoxazol-5(4 H )-one
items.description: This scheme illustrates the three-component coupling reaction of an aromatic aldehyde, ethyl acetoacetate, and hydroxylamine hydrochloride in GAAS to produce 3,4-disubstituted isoxazol-5(4H)-ones.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of reaction solvent and GAAS (50 wt%) at different conditions
items.description: This table details the screening of various solvents, temperatures, and reaction times to optimize the yield of the model reaction.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Synthesis of the 3-Methyl-4-arylmethylene isoxazol-5(4 H )-one
items.description: This table summarizes the substrate scope for various aromatic and heterocyclic aldehydes, providing reaction times, yields, and melting points for products 4a-4k.

items.heading: Table 3
items.caption: Recyclability study of the GAAS (50 wt %)
items.description: This table shows the performance of the GAAS medium over four consecutive reaction cycles, demonstrating its stability and reusability.

items.heading: Table 4
items.caption: Comparison for different green catalysts or reaction mediums used for synthesis of 3,4-disubstituted isoxazol-5(4 H )-ones
items.description: A comparative analysis of the current GAAS method against previously reported green catalysts in terms of temperature, time, and yield.
